title: Primitive recursion: functions built by finite iteration

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems
based_on.pages: 96–104, 106–112 (§§14.1–14.4 and 14.6–14.7; second edition, corrected reprint August 2020)

summary: Build numerical functions from composition and finite iteration, then prove that bounded tests and bounded searches stay within the same class.
abstract: Testing whether a natural number is a square requires only finitely many candidate roots, but a precise computability claim must also explain how the tests and the search are built. Primitive recursion supplies a class of guaranteed terminating calculations: start with zero, successor and selection of inputs, then combine functions and repeat a defined step a prescribed number of times. Arithmetic operations and equality tests can be constructed within this class. Testing or searching a specified finite range stays within it whenever the underlying tests are already primitive recursive. Bounded search returns its first witness or reports that the range was exhausted, supporting division with remainder and square-root tests. These results turn finite-loop descriptions into explicit constructions of numerical functions whose termination follows from the construction rules.
